But when they shared, the bounty multiplied, turning the desert into a paradise. Thus, the law of the harvest was written: to grow, one must give, and to receive, one must return. In this cycle, the prosperity of the one is bound to the kindness of the other, forever entwined.

If he kept them, they remained mere pebbles. If he cast them into the depths, they tripled in number, but he relied on Luna to share the bounty.

In the garden of trust, the harvest is infinite, but in the garden of greed, the ground turns to dust.
